hypothesis: The fmt=1 per-row int8 dense GEMV gives one block to one output row, so every block reads the whole activation vector: a call moves I*O weight bytes and I*O*4 activation bytes, and four fifths of its traffic is x. Giving a block R output rows should read x once per R rows and cut total traffic from 5x the weight bytes to (1 + 4/R)x. The same kernel also issues R*U independent weight loads before consuming any, because Nsight Compute measures the original as memory-latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound (occupancy 91.9 %, DRAM throughput 34.6 %, 60 % of a 27-cycle issue gap stalled on an L1TEX scoreboard). Both changes are in the same kernel and this record cannot separate them.

quality.method: Not a numerical arm: quant_matmul_i8r keeps the original summation order (i = t, t+256, ... ascending), the same 256-wide reduction tree and the same trailing f32 scale, so its output is bitwise identical to this arm's and the comparison cannot be confounded by a quality difference. c/tests/test_int8_rows_cuda.cu asserts exactly that with memcmp on trunk geometry, on S > 1 and on the short-block shapes (O = 13, 5, 17, 3, 1), against a double-precision CPU reference, with a mutated-weight probe so that identity between two kernels that read nothing would fail. That test was last executed on an earlier commit of this branch and has NOT been re-run on the commit recorded here; it needs a GPU and one has not been available since.
Same as the baseline: the two arms are bitwise identical by construction and by test, so this record's only open quality item is re-running c/tests/test_int8_rows_cuda.cu on the recorded commit.
